ID: `fixing-motion-performance`.

## What it does

Classifies motion costs as compositing, painting or layout recalculation. Looks for interleaved DOM reads and writes, scroll polling, animated inherited variables, large blurs and endless loops. Prefers less expensive properties and measurements collected before animation. Keeps the existing library and verifies layers when performance is part of the problem.

## When to use it

Use it for stuttering transitions, slow gestures or animations that deteriorate during loading and scrolling. It corrects the technical cost of an effect; the aesthetic direction remains in the brief.

## How to use it

Ask for it by name, or invoke it with `/fixing-motion-performance` in Claude Code or `$fixing-motion-performance` in Codex. Specify the component, interaction, reproduction conditions and animation system. Ask to find the cause before changing values. Request an alternative that preserves behavior and a test under the conditions where the defect appeared.

## What it delivers

- Cause and affected fragments
- Technical alternative and bounded change
- Results of the available performance test

## Example

The drawer stutters while we load data. Analyze layout reads and animated properties, apply a targeted correction and retest under load.
